en.title: Communities abroad
en.summary: English speakers who live outside their home country, and migrants who learn English.

paragraphs: Millions of English speakers live outside their home country. This lesson describes expatriate and migrant communities and teaches you to talk about how long you have lived somewhere.

Many British people retire to Spain, France or Portugal, and large numbers of Americans work in Europe, Asia and the Middle East. These expatriates, or expats, often form communities with their own clubs, libraries and churches. At the same time, millions of people from India, China, Africa and Latin America have moved to English-speaking countries and learned English as a second language. A woman talks to a friend about her life abroad.

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: I have lived in Spain for ten years. I moved with my husband when we retired.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: Is there an English community there?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Yes, quite a large one. We have clubs, a library and a church. But I also try to learn Spanish.

lines.speaker: Friend
lines.text: That is wise. Do your neighbours speak English?

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: Some do, but most don't, so I'm learning. It's not easy at my age!

lines.speaker: Woman
lines.text: A few. We have met for coffee every Friday since last spring.

paragraphs: **1. The present perfect with for and since.** For gives the length of time; since gives the starting point. Both describe a situation that is still true now. See Introduction to Grammar: Past tenses.

blocks.html:
FormExample
have lived forI have lived in Spain for ten years.
has been sinceShe has been here since 2015.
How long...?How long have you lived there?
haven't + sinceI haven't seen him since June.

paragraphs: **2. Country, adjective and person.** Learn all three forms: the country, the adjective, and the word for a person. See Introduction to Grammar: Adjectives.

items: An expatriate (expat) lives abroad for work or retirement.
A migrant moves to another country to settle there.
Large English-speaking communities live in Spain, France and the United Arab Emirates.
Retire means stop working because of age.

paragraphs: Many migrants to Britain and the United States keep their first language at home, so large cities have many languages. Public libraries and community centres often run English classes and conversation groups.
